Subject: LazyBird v2 tokenizer edge case — temporary pin request & rollout questions

Team —

Quick summary: during the Acme AI integration smoke tests this morning we observed a tokenizer boundary mismatch for LazyBird v2 that causes downstream prompt truncation / shifted entity alignment on a subset (~0.7%) of real-world prompts (examples in attached PDF). Acme's webhook tests surfaced this and they're blocked from going live next week unless we stabilise their integration.

Ask: I'd like to request a temporary version pin (hosted API + Dedicated routing) to LazyBird v1.9 for Acme while we remediate v2. Specific asks:
- Compatibility check: can infra/serving validate whether a compatibility shim or alternate tokeniser variant will eliminate the failure modes? (Dev/Soojin)
- Fallback variant: evaluate and publish a short-lived variant (lazybird-v2-legacy-tokenizer or lazybird-v1.9-route) we can route to via policy. (Dev/Marcus)
- Telemetry: add a custom counter and sample traces for affected token/offset mismatches. (Marcus)
- Rollout & canary: propose a 72-hour temporary pin with a canary at 5% for the first 6 hours, then full pin if no regressions. (Laura/Soojin)
- Customer impact: Acme needs a clear ETA to finish integration. I'll coordinate comms once we have signoff.

Attachments: lazybird_v2_token_report.pdf (examples + repro), fallback_variant_matrix.csv (initial idea), temp_pin_playbook.docx (proposed steps).

Deadline: Can you respond with recommended course and owners by EOB today? Acme's PM (Julia) is cc'd and would like a short ETA.

Thanks —
Naomi

Subject: Re: LazyBird v2 tokenizer edge case — temporary pin request & rollout questions

Thanks Naomi — dug into the attached report and ran local reproductions against the v2 tokenizer. TL;DR: v2 changed the BPE merge ordering and introduced a small byte-level heuristic to better handle edge Unicode sequences. That heuristic shifts token boundaries for very long concatenated identifiers (the exact class Acme is hitting), which shifts offsets in downstream span extraction.

Options I see (with rough estimates):
1) Compatibility shim (recommended short-term): compile a v2 runtime variant that forces legacy BPE ordering and the old heuristic. This yields functional parity for token offsets but increases decode CPU by ~6% and raises memory for KV cache by ~3%. Build + deploy ~8–12 hours.
2) Route to v1.9 (cleanest): pin requests from Acme to v1.9 while we patch v2. No runtime changes but loses any v2 latency improvements. Routing + policy change ~1 hour, needs a short rollback playbook.
3) Full v2 fix upstream: change tokenizer logic and re-run model certification — that's a multi-day patch and not acceptable for next-week go-live.

I'm leaning to option (2) for speed, with a queued task to build option (1) in case we need a v2-compatible artifact for customers that require v2 features. I've attached a fallback_variant_matrix.csv with resource deltas and a suggested canary schedule.

If we pin to v1.9 for 72 hours, we should:
- Add a lightweight header in responses (X-Model-Pinned: v1.9) so clients know routing (Marcus)
- Create a short-lived canary route and monitor alignment counters for the next 24 hours (Marcus + Laura)
- Capture failing prompts to a gated bucket (PII-safe scrub) for dev triage

I can start the routing change once Naomi signs off.

—Dev
Senior Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime

Subject: Re: LazyBird v2 tokenizer edge case — temporary pin request & rollout questions

Adding infra/ops perspective and a few logistics:

- Canary plan: 5% traffic for 6 hours -> 20% for next 12 hours -> 100% pin. We should gate the 20% step on the alignment counter not exceeding baseline.
- Routing: we can implement a policy-scoped pin for Acme's API key only; that avoids global impact. That policy change is low-risk but requires a signed change and a short blameless post-mortem if rollback occurs.
- Telemetry & storage: Marcus, we need the exact sample rate for stored failed prompts. Security wants PII scrubbing before storage.
- JIRA: created INF-3421 for the remediation task and INF-3422 for telemetry.

External note for Acme (Julia) — we can pin you to v1.9 in <4 hours once we have internal signoff and a confirmed SCM change window. We'll keep the pin temporary and reversible; expect an operations message when the pin is live.

Soojin
Operations Engineering

Subject: Re: LazyBird v2 tokenizer edge case — temporary pin request & rollout questions

Thanks all — based on Dev + Soojin recommendations I approve the following immediate plan:

1) Temporary pin Acme API key -> lazybird-v1.9 (policy-scoped) for 72 hours from pin time.
2) Canary: 5% for 6h, then evaluate; proceed to 20% only if alignment counters are within baseline; full 100% pin if green after 18h.
3) Telemetry: Marcus to instrument alignment counter and sampling hooks; capture failing prompts to a scrubbed bucket (INF-3422).
4) Compatibility artifact: Dev to queue the compatibility-shim build (option 1) and prioritize it after the pin.
5) Comms: I will notify Acme that we will pin immediately and provide a 72-hour ETA and daily update cadence.

Owners & timelines:
- Dev: prepare queued compatibility artifact (start today, estimate 24–36h dev + 8–12h deploy)
- Soojin: implement policy-scoped pin and canary schedule (target: pin live within 4 hours)
- Marcus: telemetry + X-Model-Pinned header (by canary start)
- Laura: monitor dashboards and author go/no-go at the 6h and 18h checks

Julia — thanks for flagging this early. Expect a confirmation email when the pin is live and a short status update at T+6h and T+18h.

I'll update INF-3421 with this plan and close the pin window if we remediate v2 earlier.

Best,
Naomi
